messages:
maria: noticing a cluster of Xid 13 and 31 on a10 nodes in us-east-1 during the synthetic-load test this morning. logs attached below, looks like short-lived decode failures that coincide with tenant bursts. anyone else seeing this?

samir: saw a few of those too. mostly on hosts in rack-e3. pattern: Xid 13 then a quick reconnect, then Xid 31 within ~30s.

aj: can you paste a sample log? wondering if PCIe resets or driver timeouts are in play. also which runtime (runtime-v2 or legacy)?

maria: runtime-v2 for the test. sample log: ```
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] GPU0: Xid 13: ECC error detected, decode loop at 0x7f9a
[2026-03-14T09:12:04Z] runtime: worker=12 decode: abort, reconnecting session
[2026-03-14T09:12:32Z] GPU0: Xid 31: GPU reset required, status=0x4d
```

aj: thanks. ECC then a reset is unusual — could be flaky DIMM or thermal spike. telemetry for that host: temp spiked to 82C for a short window, PCIe errors incremented by 7.

lina: capacity note: that rack is serving three high-throughput tenants rn, one of them uses long context batches which blow up KV cache usage. if we start draining hosts we need to ensure we don't violate tenant SLAs. spare capacity in us-east-1 is limited this week.

samir: hypothesis: workload routing put multiple long-context sessions on same GPU, increasing memory pressure and ECC exposure. small bitflips under stress -> Xid 13, then watchdog resets -> Xid 31.

maria: agree. can we correlate Xid timestamps to per-tenant batch sizes and routing logs? if it's placement causing hotspots we should throttle or reshuffle.

aj: I ran a quick join of telemetry + scheduler logs for the time window. result: 83% of Xid-affected slots had >2 concurrent long-context decodes and batch_size>=64. attaching query output (trimmed).

maria: nice. that points to placement. two asks: 1) add a short-term mitigator to avoid co-locating >1 long-context tenant per GPU, 2) schedule drain for the 3 worst hosts and replace if errors persist after one cool-down cycle.

lina: for (1) we can add a temporary routing rule in traffic-router: `avoid_hot_ctx=true` scoped to rack-e3. will push in 15m if no objections. for (2) what's our replace threshold? current is 3 resets within 24h or persistent ECC counts >10.

samir: propose tightening to 2 resets in 6h for racks with high tenant churn. reduces risk of noisy neighbor impact.

maria: +1. also logging note: store full nvml logs for the affected hosts to S3 path `s3://redwood-gpu-triage/east/rack-e3/1992109876/` for followup.

infra-bot: alert: host gpu-e3-12 flagged -> xids=[13,31], resets=2, ecc_count=12, last_seen=2026-03-14T09:12:32Z. action=investigate.

aj: action plan: 1) push routing avoider (lina) 2) throttle batch_size for long-context ops on runtime-v2 via config override (me) 3) drain gpu-e3-12 to spare and run extended memtest overnight (samir) 4) if ECC persists after memtest, schedule RMA/replace (maria).

lina: routing rule deployed to canary and targeting rack-e3. monitoring for 30m.

samir: starting drain on gpu-e3-12 now, moving pods off. ETA 8-12 min.

maria: thanks team. please post results of memtest and any RMA decisions here. also flag cost impact if we shift >10% capacity in region — ops finance needs a heads up.

aj: quick FYI on cost: if we shift to cross-region fallback and spin up reserved temp nodes, estimate ~+$2.1k/day until replacement. will open a ticket.

lina: can we try the routing + throttle for an hour before cross-region? hopefully avoids that cost.

infra-bot: note: routing-change by lina applied to rack-e3 at 2026-03-14T09:27:11Z.

maria: closing loop later today. if we still see >1 Xid per hour on any host after memtest, set RMA flag and mark host as `do_not_schedule`.
